issue: Clause-final 'oleh adik' after a time adverb is written-register for a mundane family chore; in speech the kin agent sits right after the di- verb with no oleh (cf. id-0814's own tip).

fix.target: Sampahnya sudah dibuang adik tadi pagi.
fix.english: The trash was already taken out by my little brother this morning.

issue: Same oleh-overuse pattern: 'disiram setiap sore oleh ayah' is news-prose ordering; conversational Indonesian puts the short kin agent directly after the verb: 'disiram ayah setiap sore'.

fix.english: The plants are watered by Dad every afternoon.

issue: 'di bawah matahari' is an English calque of 'under the sun'; natives say 'di bawah sinar/terik matahari' or simply 'dijemur di luar' (jemur already implies sun-drying).

fix.target: Kasurnya dijemur di luar supaya tidak lembap.
fix.english: The mattress is put out to dry so it doesn't get damp.
fix.grammar: supaya = so that: dijemur supaya tidak lembap = dried so it doesn't get damp.

issue: 'bisa diminta gratis' is unnatural — you ambil/dapat a free map, you don't 'request it free'; and the -nya definite marker (the node's teaching point) is glossed indefinite 'A city map', contradicting the pattern.

fix.target: Peta kotanya bisa diambil gratis di lobi hotel.
fix.english: The city map can be picked up for free in the hotel lobby.

issue: Gloss mismatch: 'Karyawan baru itu' is a specific person and the sentence reads as completed narrative, but the English 'The new employee is trained during...' reads as a generic company policy.

fix.target: Karyawan baru itu dilatih selama dua minggu pertama.
fix.english: That new employee was trained for the first two weeks.

issue: 'dicuci bersama' is ambiguous — it reads 'washed together (with someone)' rather than the intended 'washed in one load'; the idiomatic word is 'sekaligus'.

fix.target: Pakaian kotor dikumpulkan dulu sebelum dicuci sekaligus.
fix.english: The dirty clothes are gathered first before being washed all at once.

sekaligus.en: all at once; in one go

issue: Gloss fidelity: 'barangnya' is general belongings/stuff, not specifically 'the bags' — the English narrows the meaning and would back-translate as 'tasnya'.

fix.target: Tolong dijaga barangnya, saya ke toilet sebentar.
fix.english: Please keep an eye on my things; I'm going to the toilet for a moment.

issue: 'janjinya dengan anak-anak' means an appointment/plan made WITH the kids, but the gloss says 'the promise TO the kids' (that would be 'janji kepada'); on top of that 'jangan dilupakan' with an abstract object is stiff — jangan+di- suits concrete requests.

fix.target: Jangan dibatalkan janjinya dengan anak-anak besok.
fix.english: Don't cancel the plans with the kids tomorrow.

issue: 'gedung seni' is not an Indonesian collocation — the fixed terms are 'gedung kesenian' or, for where a dancer actually trains, 'sanggar (tari)'.

fix.target: Penari muda itu berlatih setiap sore di sanggar tari.
fix.english: That young dancer practices every afternoon at the dance studio.

issue: Referential clash: distal 'Pembantu rumah tangga itu' (that helper, someone else's) cooking 'untuk keluarga kami' (for OUR family) — a native would say 'pembantu kami'; 'itu' + 'kami' don't sit together.

fix.target: Pembantu kami memasak makanan untuk seluruh keluarga.
fix.english: Our helper cooks food for the whole family.

issue: Gloss calque: 'lebih berat' for training means tougher/harder; 'This morning's practice is heavier' is unidiomatic English carried over word-for-word from berat.

fix.target: Latihan pagi ini lebih berat daripada latihan kemarin.
fix.english: This morning's practice was tougher than yesterday's practice.

issue: Register clash: formal 'atas' + bare casual 'kamu' ('atas bantuan kamu') is a mix natives avoid — the natural forms are 'atas bantuanmu' or 'atas bantuannya'.

fix.target: Terima kasih banyak atas bantuanmu minggu lalu.
fix.english: Thank you very much for your help last week.
fix.grammar: bantu (help, verb) → bantuan (help, noun): the aid that is given.

issue: 'di bawah matahari' is the same 'under the sun' calque as id-0825; for overheating the idiomatic phrase is 'di bawah terik matahari' (under the scorching sun).

fix.target: Dia kepanasan karena berdiri lama di bawah terik matahari.
fix.english: He got overheated because he stood for a long time under the scorching sun.
